newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: BIS invites ex-Yugo republics to join, not Belgrade.
newsitem.headline: BIS invites ex-Yugo republics to join, not Belgrade.

text.p: The Bank for International Settlements (BIS) said it has decided to invite the central banks of Bosnia, Croatia, Macedonia and Slovenia to become members.

BIS said its board of directors, consisting of central bank governors from the Group of Ten (G10) industrialised countries, had invited the central banks of the four former Yugoslav republics to subscribe to shares in the international organisation of central banks.
BIS said the invitation was an interim solution while the four states and rump Yugoslavia continue talks on dividing the assets of former Yugoslavia's central bank.
The National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY), the remaining central bank for rump Yugoslavia which consists of Serbia and Montenegro, was not invited to join the BIS.
BIS provides financial services for central banks and is also a forum for direct contact among central bankers on monetary policy issues.

Former Yugoslavia has assets of around $660 million at the BIS. The voting rights attached to the 8,000 BIS shares held by former Yugoslavia were suspended in June 1992 as a result of the violent breakup of the Balkan state in 1991.
BIS and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) have proposed dividing former Yugoslavia's assets between today's five independent states according to a formula, which has not yet been agreed.
Talks among the five states on how to divide the assets are still going on.
Once an agreement is reached, the new BIS shares for the four independent states will be cancelled and the suspended shares of former Yugoslavia will be divided among them and rump Yugoslavia.

At a meeting last July, central bank governors from Bosnia, Croatia, Macedonia and Slovenia supported the BIS plan for splitting the assets of former Yugoslavia. Rump Yugoslavia's NBY was invited to the meeting but did not attend.
